title: Chapter 12 – Sample Arbiter Exam Questions: Mock Exam

questions.text: What score must a candidate achieve to pass the FIDE Arbiter seminar exam?
questions.explanation: As per Article 12.1 and B06.1.3, a candidate must pass the FIDE Arbiter seminar exam with a score of at least 80% to qualify for the FA title application.

questions.text: Which topics are covered by Laws of Chess exam questions?

options.text: Only Articles 1 to 5
Only the arbiter's powers and penalties
All 12 articles including touch-move, illegal moves, draws, clocks and late arrival
Only rating and title regulations

questions.explanation: As per Article 12.2, exam questions on Laws of Chess cover all 12 articles including touch-move rule, illegal moves, draw claims, clock handling, late arrival, move recording, and arbiter authority.

questions.text: What does an anti-cheating question in the FIDE Arbiter exam typically cover?

options.text: How to detect illegal moves during a game
Fair Play Regulations, the Fair Play Officer's role, investigation procedures and sanctions
The procedure for using a chess engine to verify results
How to search players for electronic devices

questions.explanation: As per Article 12.6, anti-cheating questions cover the FIDE Fair Play Regulations including the Fair Play Officer's authority, investigation procedures, use of statistical analysis, and available sanctions.

questions.text: What do practical scenario questions in the arbiter exam test?

options.text: Only memorisation of article numbers
Knowledge of chess openings
Both knowledge of rules and sound arbiter judgment in real-life situations
The ability to calculate rating changes manually

questions.explanation: As per Article 12.5, practical scenario questions present real-life arbiting situations and test both rules knowledge and sound judgment. The correct answer must demonstrate both aspects.

questions.text: What must arbiter candidates know about rating and title questions in the exam?

options.text: Only the rating of the top 10 players in the world
K-factors, performance rating calculation, norm requirements and reporting procedures
Only how to submit a rating report online
The FIDE rating of each titled player

questions.explanation: As per Article 12.4, rating and title questions test knowledge of K-factors, performance rating calculation, norm requirements, reporting procedures, and the differences between standard, rapid and blitz rating systems.

questions.text: A player's flag falls at the end of their move. The position is a theoretical draw. What should the arbiter rule?

options.text: Draw, because the position is theoretically drawn
The player whose flag fell loses the game
The game is a draw only if the opponent also cannot deliver checkmate
The arbiter must pause the clock and analyse the position

questions.explanation: Per Article 6.10, if a player's flag falls (time runs out), the game is lost — regardless of the position, UNLESS the opponent cannot possibly deliver checkmate. In a theoretical draw where checkmate IS still possible with any sequence of legal moves, the player who ran out of time loses.

questions.text: During a game, White completes an illegal move (pawn moved backward). The arbiter notices. What is the correct procedure?

options.text: The game continues — the illegal move stands since both players continued
White loses the game immediately for any illegal move
The arbiter resets the position, the opponent gains 2 extra minutes (or game loss for 2nd offence)
White must replay the move with the same piece only

questions.explanation: Per Article 7.4, after an illegal move is completed (clock pressed), the arbiter resets the position to before the illegal move, the opponent receives 2 extra minutes of thinking time, and the offending player must make a legal move. A second illegal move by the same player results in loss of the game.

questions.text: Black claims a draw by insufficient mating material when only kings remain. The arbiter checks and also sees it is now White's move with a lone rook on the board. What should the arbiter do?

options.text: Uphold the draw claim — with only kings the game is always a draw
Reject the draw claim — White has a rook and can potentially deliver checkmate
Pause the game and ask both players if they agree to a draw
Award Black the win since their king survived

questions.explanation: Per Article 9.6, a draw by insufficient mating material applies only when it is impossible to checkmate with any sequence of legal moves. A rook and king CAN deliver checkmate, so the draw claim must be rejected and play continues.

questions.text: A player is caught with a vibrating device in their pocket during a game. They claim it is a medical device. What should the arbiter do?

options.text: Accept the explanation and allow the player to continue
Apply the default penalty (loss of game) unless the competition rules state otherwise, and report to the Chief Arbiter
Give a formal warning and ask the player to remove the device
Suspend the game and consult FIDE by email

questions.explanation: Per Article 11.2, having an electronic device on one's person during play results in loss of the game. Medical exceptions may be granted but only if declared BEFORE the game and approved by the Chief Arbiter. A claim made after discovery does not override the rule.

questions.text: A player writes their intended move on the scoresheet before making it, then claims a draw by threefold repetition. Is the claim valid?

options.text: No — writing a move before playing it is illegal
Yes — the player must write the move on the scoresheet and stop the clock to claim the threefold repetition correctly
Yes — but only if the repetition has already happened three times before writing the move
No — the arbiter must verify the repetition independently before allowing the claim

questions.explanation: Per Article 9.3, to claim a draw by threefold repetition when the position is ABOUT TO appear for the third time, the player must first write the intended move on the scoresheet without making it, then stop the clock and inform the arbiter. This is the only correct procedure.
